items.title: Freeze interfaces: manifests, Rational qty core, shared types, DB schema, tokens, sqlite smoke
items.acceptance: All downstream modules can import a frozen contract surface — Rational quantity type, recipe/step/score-breakdown/cooking-event shapes, household-scoped DB helpers over a real SQLite file, and the design tokens — with the repo typechecking strictly and running .ts directly on Node 24 with zero runtime dependencies.
items.notes: Runs ALONE; owns the manifests (sole exception to the manifest exclusion). Invariant 1: Rational (bigint num/den) is the ONLY arithmetic type on authoritative paths, qty.ts the sole entry point, rounding once at display/package boundary. Invariant 2: cooking-event shape stores timers as absolute UTC end instants, never remaining-seconds. Invariant 3: every db.ts helper takes household_id as REQUIRED first argument and appends the WHERE itself — an unscoped query must be inexpressible. Schema includes a separate never-overwritten column for user grocery-quantity edits [steal C]. tsc --noEmit is the gate, never a build step; devDependency typescript only. Smoke check proves node:sqlite on a real file DB with the actual statement API. tokens.css: type scale, 4px grid, dark-first verified contrast, 44px targets, focus states, prefers-reduced-motion, tabular-nums.

items.title: Build units, ingredient normalization with aliases, and curated ingredient conversion tables
items.acceptance: Ingredient text variants (including the garlic alias family: 'garlic cloves', 'cloves of garlic', 'fresh garlic', '3 cloves garlic, minced') normalize to one canonical ingredient id with a confidence value, and same-dimension conversions land in grams/millilitres/count while cross-dimension conversion happens only via curated density or per-item weight and is otherwise reported separately, never guessed.
items.notes: Invariant 1 binds: all arithmetic through qty.ts Rational; review greps for bare +/* on numbers in these files. 'To taste' is a distinct non-numeric state, never foldable into a quantity. Ranges preserved as min/max, scaled independently. CYCLE 6 (D-9): domain/src/ingredients.ts CUT — catalog.ts already owns the curated registry; a second table would be a second source of truth.

items.title: Build serving scaling and cross-recipe aggregation with full line-level traceability
items.acceptance: Requirements from multiple recipes scaled to target servings merge into single lines only when canonical ingredient id AND base-unit dimension match, every aggregated number carries links back to each contributing recipe line and amount, and the four garlic alias fixture forms produce exactly one aggregated line.
items.notes: Invariant 1 binds: Rational only, no floats. Scale factor = target_servings / servings_default applied to min and max independently. Differing preparation states preserved on the line, never silently merged. Traceability is a data structure produced here, not a UI afterthought — DoD 5's test asserts these links exist for every line.

items.title: Build confidence-gated inventory subtraction and package selection with surplus math
items.acceptance: purchase_requirement = max(0, aggregated − usable_inventory) subtracting only confirmed/assumed_staple entries (less-certain entries become confirmation-question objects, never silent subtractions), and the chosen package combination's total yield always covers the requirement — underbuying impossible — minimising (expected waste, package count), with expected_surplus computed and generic fallbacks ('one bunch', 'one ~2 lb package') flagged as estimates.
items.notes: Invariant 1 binds: Rational only; rounding once at the package boundary. Ranges purchased conservatively (against max). Surplus is a value returned for write-on-purchase-confirmation, not written here (domain stays pure). Confirmation questions are high-value and few, never a pantry review.

items.title: Build attribute-level preference model, feedback updates, and variance-selecting calibration
items.acceptance: Every calibration reaction and post-meal feedback event updates per-attribute signals (protein, cuisine, flavour, texture, spice, richness, method, effort) each carrying value, confidence and durability — never one opaque score — with negative signals weighted more strongly and faster than weak positives, and the calibration module deliberately SELECTS 8–15 cards for maximum attribute spread rather than sampling randomly.
items.notes: Card selection variance is why candidate B won — the spec demands deliberately varied cards, not just reactions. Four reactions: looks good / not for me / never recommend / too much work; 'never recommend' feeds the hard-exclusion set consumed by filters. Persisted score/signal values go through Rational on authoritative paths (Invariant 1).

items.title: Build absolute hard filters and configurable weighted scoring with persisted breakdowns
items.acceptance: Allergies, dietary restrictions, explicit exclusions, hard time ceilings and recent-repeat constraints eliminate recipes absolutely before any scoring, and survivors receive a score of 0.32 preference + 0.20 context/interruption + 0.16 inventory + 0.12 cost + 0.10 novelty + 0.10 leftover-usefulness minus explicit penalties, with weights in one config object and a full per-recipe breakdown persisted.
items.notes: Hard-constraint precedence is absolute and never averaged: allergy > household hard restriction > member hard restriction > strong dislike > soft preference > optimisation. A strong dislike can never be outweighed by inventory use or cost. Adjacent novelty = attribute distance with at least one familiar anchor preserved. No LLM anywhere. Invariant 1 binds on persisted scores. CYCLE 6: builder was killed mid-wave before writing tests/score.test.ts; behaviour verified by the conductor gate instead, and the missing regression tests are filed as T-029.

items.title: Build greedy set-scoring planset and frozen-context swap
items.acceptance: The planset pass optimises the SET of three meals for ingredient overlap, protein and cuisine diversity, total weekly active time and cost, and a swap by explicit reason (faster, less hands-on, fewer dishes, cheaper, more familiar, more adventurous, no pasta, different protein, use what I have) returns at most three alternatives ranked against the two untouched meals — which are provably unchanged.
items.notes: Invariant 4 binds and is the whole point: swap re-ranks against the FROZEN remaining two meals and NEVER re-runs planset. An agent who 'helpfully' re-optimises the set breaks DoD 3. Greedy set pass per D-2 (combinatorial search is a non-goal tonight).

items.title: Build catalog validation gate, ingredient registry, and allergen-class cross-check
items.acceptance: A recipe is ineligible for recommendation unless quantities are complete, steps ordered, servings known, dietary tags verified, and all nine per-step interruption-metadata fields present — and every recipe ingredient id resolves in the registry with its allergen classes consistent with the recipe's dietary tags, so an allergen can never hide behind an unverified tag.
items.notes: FROZEN CONTRACT (cycle 3, T-001 landed): the nine per-step interruption fields on RecipeStep in domain/src/recipe.ts use two names that DIFFER FROM SPEC.md — `maximum_pause` (a MaximumPause union: {kind:'bounded',seconds} | {kind:'unlimited'}), NOT `maximum_pause_seconds`; and `timer_duration_seconds` (number | null), NOT `timer_duration`. Also `recovery_instruction` is a RecoveryGuidance union ({kind:'instruction',text} | {kind:'none_available'}), not a bare string. Validate against the TYPES, not against the SPEC's field names. Invariant 5 binds: this gate and the ingredient-id/allergen-class cross-check land BEFORE any recipe is authored — otherwise DoD 9 fails via data at 5am. Registry carries curated aliases, densities, per-item weights, allergen classes, store sections. The gate excludes incomplete recipes rather than failing the build, which is what makes a short catalog a graceful degradation.

items.title: Author proven first recipe batch (6 recipes, maximum attribute spread)
items.acceptance: Six recipes spanning distinct proteins, cuisines, methods and effort levels pass the full validation gate including complete quantities against registry ids, the full attribute vector, and all nine interruption-metadata fields on every step — establishing the schema-first authoring pattern the bulk batches copy.
items.notes: FROZEN CONTRACT (cycle 3): author every step against domain/src/recipe.ts RecipeStep, NOT against SPEC.md's field names. Two differ: `maximum_pause` is a union {kind:'bounded',seconds:n} | {kind:'unlimited'} (NOT `maximum_pause_seconds`), and the timer field is `timer_duration_seconds: number | null` (NOT `timer_duration`). `recovery_instruction` is {kind:'instruction',text:'...'} | {kind:'none_available'} — a real step-specific instruction or the explicit none, never a fabricated string. All nine fields are required on every step. This batch is the template: schema-first data entry against the gate, not prose. Recovery instructions must be real and step-specific (Invariant 6 consumes them verbatim). Owns numeric prefixes r01–r06 only. Include at least one very-low-effort and one adventurous recipe so calibration and swaps have range even if bulk batches slip.

items.title: Author recipe batch 2 (recipes 7–18)
items.acceptance: Twelve additional recipes pass the full validation gate and widen attribute coverage (cost bands, dish counts, unattended-heavy methods like braises/sheet-pan, spice levels) beyond batch 1.
items.notes: FROZEN CONTRACT (cycle 3): step fields follow domain/src/recipe.ts, not SPEC.md's names — `maximum_pause` union (not `maximum_pause_seconds`), `timer_duration_seconds` (not `timer_duration`), `recovery_instruction` as an instruction|none_available union. DESIGN ruling binds: FEWER FULLY-VALID RECIPES BEAT PARTIALLY-VALID ONES — if time pressures, ship fewer complete recipes rather than more incomplete ones; the gate excludes incomplete recipes anyway. Owns prefixes r07–r18 only; do not touch batch-1 or batch-3 files, the registry, or the gate.

items.title: Author recipe batch 3 (recipes 19–30)
items.acceptance: The catalog reaches ~30 gate-valid recipes with deliberate ingredient-overlap clusters (shared herbs, sauces, proteins) so planset's ingredient-overlap and leftover-usefulness terms have real signal to optimise.
items.notes: FROZEN CONTRACT (cycle 3): step fields follow domain/src/recipe.ts, not SPEC.md's names — `maximum_pause` union (not `maximum_pause_seconds`), `timer_duration_seconds` (not `timer_duration`), `recovery_instruction` as an instruction|none_available union. Same graceful-degradation ruling as T-010. Owns prefixes r19–r30 only. Runs in parallel with T-010 — coordinate nothing, just stay inside the assigned file range. If registry ingredients are missing, that is a gap to report, not a license to edit data/ingredients.json (owned by T-008).

items.title: Build cooking session state machine with absolute-instant timers and kill-safe event log
items.acceptance: A cooking session reconstructed purely from its persisted events at any later wall-clock time yields the correct current step, elapsed/remaining timer state, next safe stopping point, and continuous-attention warnings — with recovery guidance drawn only from per-step metadata and an explicit 'unavailable' state when metadata is absent.
items.notes: Invariant 2 binds: timers are absolute UTC end instants, never remaining-seconds — recovery is arithmetic, not bookkeeping, which is what makes DoD 7 provable. Invariant 6 binds: recovery/panic guidance reads required per-step metadata only, never fabricated. Pure domain: no I/O, no Date.now() inside logic (time is a parameter).

items.title: Build prep-plan derivation, reason-code copy module, and shared total-vs-active time renderer
items.acceptance: For any valid recipe, prep derivation yields ingredients to retrieve, equipment, do-ahead tasks, the first non-interruptible step, the first safe stopping point and expected active-time blocks; and every human-readable time or reason string in the product is produced by this one module with numeric slots, always rendering total and active time as separate values.
items.notes: [Steal C] binds: ONE copy module + ONE shared time renderer makes DoD 6 a property of a single helper instead of a per-screen convention, and a voice review a one-file diff. Copy is concrete and countable ('22 min total, 7 hands-on'), guilt-free, honest about uncertainty. At most three reason codes per meal, rendered as concrete copy.

items.title: Build HTTP server, all routes, and entrypoint with ephemeral-port and db-path flags
items.acceptance: Every product flow (onboarding, calibration, plan, swap, grocery list with preserved user edits and confirmation questions, purchase confirmation writing surplus, prep, cooking session events, feedback, cooked-decrement) is reachable over HTTP as thin routes over domain functions, and the entrypoint accepts port and db-path flags so a test can run it on a temp DB and free port.
items.notes: Invariant 3 binds: all data access through db.ts household-scoped helpers — routes must be unable to express an unscoped query; never inline SQL in routes. User grocery edits go to the separate never-overwritten column; regeneration must not clobber them by construction. Inventory decremented on 'cooked', never 'planned'. [Steal A]: the port/db-path flags are the stated mitigation for kill-test flake — they are first-class, not debug leftovers. node:http only, zero deps.

items.title: Build web shell, shared UI components, onboarding, and calibration screens
items.acceptance: A new user completes household setup (size, restrictions, allergies, never-recommend, proteins, cuisines, time ceilings, novelty, staples) and 8–15 four-reaction calibration cards in a one-handed, under-four-minute mobile flow with one dominant bottom-anchored action per screen and never more than three choices anywhere.
items.notes: Identity contract binds: tokens-only CSS (app.css consumes tokens.css, no free-hand values); ui.js is the SOLE source of shared components — bottom sheet, undo snackbar (undo everywhere, never a confirmation modal), aria-live timer announcer, reason chips, status-beyond-colour badges. Framework-free vanilla JS. Wave-2 parallel siblings consume ui.js — keep its component API small, boring, and stable.

items.title: Build plan screen with reasoned three-alternative swap flow
items.acceptance: The plan screen shows three dinners each with name, total AND active time separately, interruption profile, effort, at most three concrete reason codes, owned/shared ingredients, cost band and novelty indicator — and swapping one meal by explicit reason takes at most three taps, offers at most three alternatives, and visibly leaves the other two meals untouched.
items.notes: All time strings and reason copy come from the domain reasons/time-renderer module — never hand-rolled here (DoD 6 mechanism). Consume shared components from ui.js per the identity contract; do not create local variants. Builds against the wave-0 route contracts; any needed contract change is an emergency single-agent commit per the contract-drift rule.

items.title: Build grocery list screen as a ledger with provenance drawers and protected user edits
items.acceptance: The grocery list renders grouped by store section with tabular numerals, every line expands to answer 'why am I buying this?' by naming each contributing recipe and amount, inventory deducted and expected surplus, estimated packages are labelled estimated, inventory confirmation questions surface inline, and a user-edited quantity visibly survives list regeneration.
items.notes: Receipt/ledger treatment [steal C]: typography does the trust-building the traceability must-have exists for. User edits live in the separate column — the UI reads and preserves it, never writes generated values over it. Quantity edit gets an undo snackbar from ui.js, not a confirmation modal. Honest uncertainty: 'estimated' stated plainly.

items.title: Build two-tap post-meal feedback screen
items.acceptance: After cooking, a user records make-again / it-was-fine / not-again plus one optional reason in at most two taps and under five seconds, with the recorded reaction reflected in stored attribute-level preference signals.
items.notes: One dominant action; the optional reason is a second tap at most, never a form. Guilt-free copy from the shared copy module. No streaks, no engagement mechanics of any kind.

items.title: Build cooking mode and prep screens with resume-into-session recovery
items.acceptance: Cooking mode shows one large-text step at a time with one-handed completion, labelled active vs unattended intervals, background-safe timers with accessible announcements, an explicit warning (with required uninterrupted duration) before any continuous-attention step, the next safe stopping point always visible — and reopening the app mid-session after a reload or kill lands the user back on the correct step with timers correct, showing validated recovery guidance or an honest 'no guidance available'.
items.notes: Invariant 2 binds: render timer state from stored absolute UTC end instants vs now — never count down a local variable as truth. Invariant 6 binds: recovery text comes only from per-step metadata; absent metadata is stated, never fabricated. Prep screen shows retrieve/equipment/do-ahead, first non-interruptible step, first safe stopping point, active-time blocks. Build accessibility in from the start (aria-live announcer from ui.js, 44px targets); the wave-3 a11y pass does not touch these files.

items.title: Prove kill/reload survival of cooking sessions end-to-end
items.acceptance: An automated end-to-end scenario advances a real cooking session with running timers, hard-kills the server process, restarts it against the same database file, and observes identical step progress and arithmetically correct timer state — proving DoD 7 by execution, not claim.
items.notes: Uses the entrypoint's ephemeral-port and db-path flags (temp SQLite file, free port per run) — the designed mitigation for kill-test flake. Invariant 2 is what makes the post-restart assertion pure arithmetic on absolute instants; if this test wants to compare remaining-seconds snapshots, the implementation has drifted.

items.title: Prove the full product loop end-to-end with the broadened DoD sweep
items.acceptance: One automated pass through onboarding → calibration → plan → swap → grocery → feedback demonstrates: a plan reached within the interaction budget, at least two of three meals approvable in-app, a swap changing exactly one meal, every grocery line carrying complete recipe-level provenance, total and active time present as separate values in every payload carrying a time, and feedback recorded in two interactions.
items.notes: [Steal A] binds: this is the BROADENED loop test — DoD 2 (>=2 of 3 approvable) and DoD 6 (total+active in every time-carrying payload) are explicit assertions, not incidental. Swap assertion must verify the two untouched meals are byte-identical before/after (Invariant 4's observable consequence).

items.title: Fuzz generated households against hard-exclusion leaks
items.acceptance: Across many seeded, randomly generated households with random allergies, restrictions and exclusions, zero produced plans contain a hard-excluded ingredient — checked at the ingredient-id and allergen-class level via the registry, not by recipe tag alone, with failing seeds reported for reproduction.
items.notes: Checks through the same registry cross-check path Invariant 5 forced early — DoD 9 can fail via data (allergen present, tag unverified), so the fuzz must resolve ingredients to allergen classes itself rather than trusting tags. Deterministic seeding so a 4am failure is reproducible.

items.title: Prove household isolation on every entity
items.acceptance: With two populated households, no request or query path returns another household's preferences, inventory, plans, grocery lists, cooking sessions or feedback — covering every entity type in the schema, including attempts that pass a foreign household's ids directly.
items.notes: Invariant 3 binds: the tests prove the STRUCTURE (every db.ts helper requires household_id and scopes itself), not merely the absence of leaks in happy paths — include a check that no data-access surface exists outside the scoped helpers. Enumerate entities from the schema so a later table cannot silently skip coverage.

items.title: Accessibility and voice pass across wave-2 screens
items.acceptance: Every screen has screen-reader labels on all interactive elements, respects dynamic type without breakage, meets contrast on the dark-first palette, has 44px minimum targets, conveys all status beyond colour alone, announces timers accessibly, requires no gesture-only critical action, offers undo (never a confirmation modal) for every destructive-feeling action, and all copy is concrete, countable and guilt-free.
items.notes: Deliberately excludes cook.js/prep.js (owned this wave by T-019, which builds its own accessibility in). Copy fixes go into domain/src/reasons.ts ONLY if a string lives there — if so, that is a one-file diff by design; coordinate via deps, do not fork copy into screens. Tokens-only CSS rule binds: fixes adjust tokens/app.css, never inline styles.

items.title: Add panic button to cooking mode
items.acceptance: A single always-reachable control in cooking mode tells an interrupted cook exactly what to do right now — what can wait, what cannot, and for how long — using only the current step's stored interruption metadata.
items.notes: Strictly after DoD green; independently droppable. Invariant 6 binds hardest here: panic guidance is assembled from maximum_pause_seconds, safe_to_pause_*, natural_stopping_point and recovery_instruction — never generated text. If metadata is missing the button says so honestly.

items.title: Add show-the-math drawer to the plan screen
items.acceptance: Each planned meal can expand to show its persisted score breakdown — every weighted component and penalty with its value — matching the numbers the engine actually stored.
items.notes: Strictly after DoD green; independently droppable. Renders the breakdown the spec already forces score.ts to persist — an additive leaf, no engine changes. Numbers formatted via the shared renderer, tabular-nums.

items.title: Add grocery list clipboard export and use-it-up surplus suggestions
items.acceptance: The grocery list copies to the clipboard as clean plain text grouped by section, and a recorded surplus ingredient surfaces as a guilt-free chip scoring its fit against upcoming plan candidates ('the leftover half-can of coconut milk fits Thursday's curry').
items.notes: Two delighters merged because both live in grocery.js (same-wave file disjointness); if time is short ship export alone and drop the useitup half. useitup.ts is a pure leaf over persisted surplus + score data; Rational arithmetic via qty.ts (Invariant 1). Guilt-free voice binds: never 'about to waste'.

items.title: Add second-adult household preferences with minimum-acceptable-fit rule
items.acceptance: A household with a second adult holding independent preference signals never receives a plan containing a meal below the minimum acceptable fit for either adult, with both adults' hard restrictions treated as absolute.
items.notes: DESIGN names this FIRST TO CUT — it is the only delighter editing existing modules rather than adding a leaf. Any touched frozen type is a contract-drift emergency (single-agent commit). Member hard restriction sits in the existing precedence chain below household hard restriction, above strong dislike.

items.title: Commit regression tests for score.ts (weights, breakdown arithmetic, penalties)
items.acceptance: tests/score.test.ts asserts the six SPEC weights exactly, that they sum to one, that total equals the sum of weighted components minus the sum of penalties for a fixture set, that every persisted value is a Rational, and that an injected config is honoured by every component (no inlined weight literals). Suite green.
items.notes: T-006 landed score.ts with ZERO committed test coverage: the builder was killed by the harness before it wrote this file. The conductor gate (SWARM/runs/cycle-006-gate-T006.mjs) verified the behaviour at cycle 6, but that gate is not in the repo and npm test does not run it, so a weight drift would ship silently. This item closes that hole. Do NOT copy the conductor gate; write tests from SPEC. CYCLE 7 VERIFIED: conductor mutation gate killed 11/13 mutants; all six weight literals, the sum-to-one, the recomputed total, the Rational structure check and the injected-config check are genuinely drift-catching. Two mutants SURVIVED (recent_repeat penalty amount 0.15->0.05; excessive_active_time threshold 2400->999999) because the total test reads penalties back from the engine rather than pinning the config literals. Those are outside this item written acceptance -> filed as T-031, not papered over.

items.title: Align the registry name-uniqueness key with the fold used at match time
items.acceptance: Two entries whose aliases differ only by internal whitespace (e.g. "red  onion" vs "red onion") are REJECTED by parseIngredientRegistry, with a test proving it. Uniqueness is keyed on the same folded form matchIngredient indexes on, so no alias collision can reach the match index.
items.notes: Found by the cycle-6 conductor gate (check N5d). parseIngredientRegistry keys uniqueness on name.toLowerCase(); normalize.ts keys its alias index on foldIngredientText (lowercase + COLLAPSED whitespace). An alias pair differing only in internal whitespace therefore passes the parser and then silently collides in the fold index, where last-writer-wins. LATENT, not live: gate check N4 proves the shipped 97-entry registry has no such pair, so no current behaviour is wrong. It is an authoring-time trap, and DoD 4 is exactly about duplicate lines caused by naming differences.

items.title: Pin the six penalty amounts and the score thresholds against silent drift
items.acceptance: Mutating any one of the six penalty amounts in SCORE_CONFIG (recent_repeat 0.15, repeated_cuisine 0.06, repeated_format 0.04, excessive_active_time 0.08, dish_count 0.02, likely_waste 0.05), or either of the excessive_active_time_threshold_seconds (2400) and dish_count_penalty_cap (0.10) settings, turns the suite RED. Each is asserted as an exact Rational literal, and at least one fixture actually draws each penalty so a threshold change is observable in a total.
items.notes: Found by the cycle-7 conductor mutation gate (SWARM/runs/cycle-007-gate-T029.mjs), evidence in .swarm/runs/cycle-007-verify-T-029.txt. Root cause is specific and worth understanding before fixing: the total test recomputes weighted components from a SPEC_WEIGHTS literal declared in the test (which is why every weight mutant dies) but subtracts penalties by reading b.penalties[name] back from the engine (line ~360), so a penalty AMOUNT drift mutates test and engine in lockstep and stays invisible. Fix by pinning penalty literals the same way SPEC_WEIGHTS pins the weights. Do NOT weaken or rewrite the existing passing assertions; add to them. repeat_penalty_window_days and dish_count_free_allowance are already covered (both mutants died).
